lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: recipe scaling and batch cooking

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recipe scaling and batch cooking task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The task sheet provides one complete recipe with ingredient quantities listed for four servings.
safetyNotes: This task only requires written calculation; no stove, oven, or knife is used as part of the lesson.
materials: learner-local: a calculator or the ability to multiply and divide fractions by hand

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific reason a household might want to scale this recipe up to twelve servings for batch cooking rather than making the four-serving version three times, using something from your ingredient math to support your answer.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Scaling calculation accuracy: Every ingredient is correctly scaled for both the two-serving and twelve-serving versions with the math shown. | Application to batch planning: The reflection gives a specific reason for batch cooking supported by a number from the ingredient math. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner scale the same recipe to an odd serving size, such as five or seven servings, and explain how they handled at least one ingredient that no longer divides evenly.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic recipe scaling and batch cooking task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: a calculator or the ability to multiply and divide fractions by hand
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The task sheet provides one complete recipe with ingredient quantities listed for four servings.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact recipe scaling and batch cooking decision or action.
Model move 2: Before scaling, find the scaling factor you would need to go from four servings to two servings, and from four servings to twelve servings.
Model move 3: Using the two-serving scaling factor, recalculate the quantity of each ingredient in the recipe, showing the multiplication or division for each one.

Model check: Scaling calculation accuracy: Every ingredient is correctly scaled for both the two-serving and twelve-serving versions with the math shown. | Application to batch planning: The reflection gives a specific reason for batch cooking supported by a number from the ingredient math.

resources.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recipe scaling and batch cooking.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The task sheet provides one complete recipe with ingredient quantities listed for four servings.
Coach direction: Before scaling, find the scaling factor you would need to go from four servings to two servings, and from four servings to twelve servings.
Learner prompt: Write the scaling factor (as a fraction or decimal) for four servings down to two servings, and the scaling factor for four servings up to twelve servings.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using the two-serving scaling factor, recalculate the quantity of each ingredient in the recipe, showing the multiplication or division for each one.
Response 1 (t2-p1): List each ingredient's original four-serving quantity next to its new two-serving quantity, with the calculation shown for each.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Every ingredient in the original recipe has a corresponding two-serving quantity calculated.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain one specific reason a household might want to scale this recipe up to twelve servings for batch cooking rather than making the four-serving version three times, using something from your ingredient math to support your answer.

Success checks: Scaling calculation accuracy: Every ingredient is correctly scaled for both the two-serving and twelve-serving versions with the math shown. | Application to batch planning: The reflection gives a specific reason for batch cooking supported by a number from the ingredient math.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recipe scaling and batch cooking condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Scaling calculation accuracy: Every ingredient is correctly scaled for both the two-serving and twelve-serving versions with the math shown. | Application to batch planning: The reflection gives a specific reason for batch cooking supported by a number from the ingredient math..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: recipe scaling and batch cooking — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.

retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
